summary: TrainMate uses Supabase Realtime v2 postgres_changes + presence + broadcast, all driven from React hooks (useChat, usePresence, useAcceptedCompanions). There are 5 distinct channel topics: `messages-<conversationId>` (INSERT on messages), `last-read-<conversationId>-<otherUserId>` (all events on last_read), `conversations-updates-<user.id>` (all events on conversations, NO filter — refetches full list), `presence-<conversationId>` (presence + typing broadcast), and `requests-changes` (all events on requests — currently NON-FUNCTIONAL because the `requests` table is not in the `supabase_realtime` publication and the `realtime.messages` authorization policy has no branch for that topic). Realtime authorization is enforced via an RLS policy on `realtime.messages` (topics `messages-%` and `last-read-%` require the caller be a conversation participant; `conversations-updates-<uid>` is self-only). There is NO polling anywhere and NO optimistic message insert — the sender's own message returns via the realtime channel echo. Read receipts are upserted into `last_read` and propagate over the `last-read-*` channel; unread counts are computed client-side with N+1 exact-count queries. Presence is per-conversation and only active while the Chat page is mounted.

dataFlows.trigger: Any INSERT into public.messages for the open conversation (other participant, or the sender's own message echoed back)
supabaseCalls: supabase.channel(`messages-${conversationId}`)
.on('postgres_changes', { event: 'INSERT', schema: 'public', table: 'messages', filter: `conversation_id=eq.${conversationId}` })
.subscribe()
cleanup: supabase.removeChannel(channel)
dataFlows.uiBehavior: Handler appends payload.new (cast as Message) to `messages` state, deduped by id (`if (prev.some(m => m.id === next.id)) return prev;`). Chat.tsx auto-scrolls (scrollIntoView on messages change) and, if the last message sender_id !== user.id, calls markAsRead(conversationId). Note: sender's own message is NOT inserted locally — it appears via this same realtime event (no self-filtering of postgres_changes).

dataFlows.trigger: User submits the composer form (handleSendMessage), or sends an attachment-only message
supabaseCalls: supabase.from('profiles').select('name').eq('id', user.id).maybeSingle()  // display name
supabase.from('messages').insert({ conversation_id, sender_id: user.id, sender_name: displayName, text: validatedText, attachment_url, attachment_type, attachment_name, attachment_size })
supabase.from('conversations').update({ last_message: (text|preview).substring(0,255), last_message_time: new Date().toISOString() }).eq('id', conversationId)  // error NOT surfaced on failure
dataFlows.uiBehavior: sets loading=true (disables send), text is trimmed + zod-validated via messageSchema (min 1 / max 2000 chars); attachment-only uses preview '📷 Photo' or '📎 name'. On INSERT error, Chat.tsx toasts the error and restores newMessage/pendingAttachment. The sent message renders when the messages-* channel INSERT event arrives (no optimistic bubble).

dataFlows.trigger: markAsRead(conversationId) — called on Chat mount (useEffect on [conversationId, user]) and every time the messages array changes with last message sender_id !== user.id
supabaseCalls: supabase.from('last_read').upsert({ user_id: user.id, conversation_id: conversationId, timestamp: new Date().toISOString() }, { onConflict: 'user_id,conversation_id' })
setUnreadCount(prev => ({ ...prev, [conversationId]: 0 }))  // local zero-out
Receiver side: initial fetch supabase.from('last_read').select('timestamp').eq('conversation_id', cid).eq('user_id', otherUserId).maybeSingle()

Receiver side: supabase.channel(`last-read-${conversationId}-${otherUserId}`) + .on('postgres_changes', { event: '*', schema: 'public', table: 'last_read', filter: `conversation_id=eq.${conversationId}` })
dataFlows.uiBehavior: The other user's client receives the UPDATE/INSERT via the last-read-* channel, checks `row.user_id === otherUserId && row.timestamp`, sets otherUserLastRead. Chat.tsx renders each own message with `isRead = isOwn && otherReadAt >= sentAt` → CheckCheck 'Read' (sky) vs CheckCheck 'Delivered' (blue). Handler ignores the current user's own last_read row (user_id mismatch).

dataFlows.trigger: ANY INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on public.conversations (from any conversation in the whole DB — the subscription has NO row filter; RLS on realtime.messages only restricts the topic to `conversations-updates-<uid>` and self-only)
supabaseCalls: supabase.channel(`conversations-updates-${user.id}`)
.on('postgres_changes', { event: '*', schema: 'public', table: 'conversations' }, () => fetchConversations())  // no filter
fetchConversations: supabase.from('conversations').select('*').contains('participants', [user.id]).order('last_message_time', { ascending: false })
then calculateUnreadCounts(convs)
dataFlows.uiBehavior: Any conversations row change anywhere refetches the entire conversation list + recomputes unread counts. This is the mechanism by which a new message (which triggers the sendMessage conversations.update) refreshes the Chats list and the unread badge. fetchConversations is the single realtime-refresh entrypoint; the refetch itself is RLS-filtered so no cross-user data leaks, but every conversations mutation app-wide fires this refetch in every open Chat/Chats page.

dataFlows.trigger: Chat page mounts (usePresence(conversationId)) and when the other user joins/leaves the same `presence-<conversationId>` channel
supabaseCalls: supabase.channel(`presence-${conversationId}`, { config: { presence: { key: user.id } } })
.on('presence', { event: 'sync' }, ...)  // channel.presenceState() → rebuild onlineUsers keyed by user.id
.on('presence', { event: 'join' }, ({ key }) => ...)  // mark online: true
.on('presence', { event: 'leave' }, ({ key }) => ...)  // mark online: false + lastSeen: now
.subscribe(async (status) => { if (status === 'SUBSCRIBED') await channel.track({ online_at: new Date().toISOString() }) })
cleanup: supabase.removeChannel(channel)  // triggers leave to others
dataFlows.uiBehavior: onlineUsers maps presence keys (user.id) → { online }. Chat.tsx: `isUserOnline(otherUserId)` drives the header pulse dot + 'Online'/'Offline' label. Because the channel is per-conversationId and the hook only mounts on the Chat page, a user is 'online' only while their Chat page is open in that exact conversation; there is no global presence and the Chats list never shows presence. Multi-tab same-user collapses to one key.

dataFlows.trigger: Every keystroke in the composer (handleInputChange → sendTypingIndicator, no debounce/throttle)
supabaseCalls: const channel = supabase.channel(`presence-${conversationId}`);  // fresh channel instance per call
await channel.send({ type: 'broadcast', event: 'typing', payload: { userId: user.id } })
Receiver: on the same topic (the subscribed presence channel) .on('broadcast', { event: 'typing' }, ({ payload }) => ...)
dataFlows.uiBehavior: Receiver adds payload.userId to typingUsers if not present (ignores self via `payload.userId !== user.id`), then setTimeout 3000ms removes it (filter id). Chat.tsx renders <TypingIndicator userName={otherUser?.name} /> when typingUsers.length > 0 (three bouncing dots + '<name> is typing...'). Broadcast is not self-echoed, and the guard double-protects. Typing is fully realtime via Realtime Broadcast — no DB writes.

dataFlows.trigger: Any INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on public.requests affecting the current user (useAcceptedCompanions mounts — used on the Chats page)
supabaseCalls: supabase.channel('requests-changes')
.on('postgres_changes', { event: '*', schema: 'public', table: 'requests', filter: `from_user_id=eq.${user.id}` }, () => fetchAcceptedRequests())
.on('postgres_changes', { event: '*', schema: 'public', table: 'requests', filter: `to_user_id=eq.${user.id}` }, () => fetchAcceptedRequests())
fetchAcceptedRequests: supabase.from('requests').select('*').eq('from_user_id', user.id).eq('status','accepted')  +  .eq('to_user_id', user.id).eq('status','accepted')
dataFlows.uiBehavior: Refetches accepted sent+received requests and merges into `companions` (Map keyed by otherUserId, most-recent createdAt wins; direction 'sent'|'received'). CAVEAT: this realtime subscription is DEAD — `requests` is not in the supabase_realtime publication (only messages, conversations, last_read are added in migrations), and the realtime.messages authorization policy has no branch for the `requests-changes` topic. The companion list only refreshes on hook mount/remount, not live.

dataFlows.trigger: User clicks a chat card in Chats.tsx (openChat)
supabaseCalls: Find existing: conversations.find(c => participants includes user.id && otherUserId) — client-side on already-fetched state
If none (and not blocked): supabase.from('profiles').select('name').eq('id', user.id).maybeSingle()

supabase.from('conversations').insert({ participants: [user.id, otherUserId], participant_names: {...}, train_number, travel_date, last_message: '', last_message_time: new Date().toISOString() }).select().single()
navigate(`/chat/${conversationId}`, { state: { conversationId, otherUser, trainNumber, travelDate } })
Chat.tsx initial fetch: supabase.from('messages').select('*').eq('conversation_id', conversationId).order('created_at', { ascending: true })  // NO limit — full history
dataFlows.uiBehavior: If no conversation exists, creates one then routes to /chat/<id>. Conversation view shows skeleton while `loading` and messages.length === 0, else renders the full ordered history with date separators (isSameDay) and read/delivered checkmarks. Blocked pairs cannot create conversations.

supabaseCalls: supabase.rpc('soft_delete_conversation', { conv_id: conversationId, user_id_to_add: user.id })

SQL: SECURITY DEFINER plpgsql — verifies auth.uid() = user_id_to_add and caller is a participant, sets app.allow_deleted_for_update='on', then UPDATE conversations SET deleted_for = array_append(COALESCE(deleted_for,'{}'), user_id_to_add) WHERE id = conv_id AND NOT already deleted_for
dataFlows.uiBehavior: On success: useChat removes the conversation locally (setConversations filter out); on the Chat page it navigates to /chats with replace. A later message re-INSERT makes the conversation reappear (deleted_for row is hidden from RLS-based `.contains('participants', ...)` query but not from realtime refetch). Direct UPDATE of deleted_for is blocked by the prevent_conversation_tamper trigger (only allowed via the RPC).

businessRules: Messages flow: send = INSERT into public.messages then UPDATE public.conversations (last_message truncated to 255 chars + last_message_time). There is NO optimistic local insert; the sender's own message arrives back through the `messages-<conversationId>` realtime INSERT event (postgres_changes is not self-filtered).

Inserted message fields: conversation_id, sender_id, sender_name (display name fetched from profiles; fallback 'User'), text (trimmed; zod messageSchema min 1 / max 2000 chars), attachment_url/attachment_type/attachment_name/attachment_size. created_at is NOT set client-side — it is server-defaulted to now() (timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()).

Attachments: uploaded to storage bucket `chat-attachments` at path `<conversationId>/<crypto.randomUUID()>.<ext>`, then a 1-year signed URL is stored as attachment_url; allowed files are images (any) or PDF/DOC/DOCX/TXT up to 10 MB.

Read receipts: markAsRead upserts `last_read` with onConflict 'user_id,conversation_id' (UNIQUE(user_id, conversation_id)); fires on Chat mount and whenever the last message is from the other user. A message shows 'Read' iff `isOwn && otherUserLastRead >= sentAt`, else 'Delivered'.

Unread counts are computed client-side per conversation (N+1): read user's last_read timestamp; if none, count messages where conversation_id = X AND sender_id != user.id (exact head-count); if present, count messages with created_at > last_read_timestamp AND sender_id != user.id; errors default to 0. Recalculated only inside fetchConversations (initial + conversations-updates realtime). getTotalUnreadCount() sums all conversations.

The conversations-updates channel subscribes to the whole conversations table with no filter — every conversations row change in the DB triggers a full refetch of the user's list (RLS-filtered for safety but heavy).

Presence is per-conversation and only live while the Chat page is mounted: `presence-<conversationId>` with presence key = user.id, track({online_at}) on SUBSCRIBED, join→online, leave→offline+lastSeen, sync→full rebuild. 'Other user online' = isUserOnline(otherUserId). Leaving the page removes the channel and broadcasts leave.

Typing is realtime Broadcast on the same `presence-<conversationId>` topic, sent on every keystroke (unthrottled), auto-cleared after a 3s setTimeout per user; the sender never sees their own indicator (broadcast is not self-echoed and the handler filters payload.userId !== user.id).

Accepted-companions realtime is dead in this codebase: `requests` is not in the supabase_realtime publication (only messages, conversations, last_read are added via ALTER PUBLICATION) and the realtime.messages authorization policy has no `requests-changes` branch — the two `.on('postgres_changes')` listeners will never fire, so the companions list updates only on mount.

Realtime authorization is enforced via RLS on realtime.messages ('Authenticated users can receive their conversation messages'): topic LIKE 'messages-%' → is_conversation_participant(replace(topic,'messages-','')::uuid); topic LIKE 'last-read-%' → is_conversation_participant(substring(topic from 11 for 36)::uuid); topic = 'conversations-updates-' || auth.uid() → self only. presence/broadcast channels are NOT gated by this policy.
last_read has REPLICA IDENTITY FULL so UPDATE/DELETE postgres_changes payloads carry the conversation_id needed to evaluate the `conversation_id=eq.` filter.

last_read table RLS only exposes the user's OWN row ('Users can view own last_read'), so the initial fetch of the other user's last_read returns null (read receipts begin at null on open); they populate only when the other user upserts while both are subscribed.

soft_delete_conversation(conv_id uuid, user_id_to_add uuid) is SECURITY DEFINER; refuses non-self (auth.uid() must equal user_id_to_add), requires the caller be a participant, and appends to conversations.deleted_for via app.allow_deleted_for_update bypassing the prevent_conversation_tamper trigger (which blocks any direct deleted_for UPDATE).

Conversation open/creation: openChat reuses an existing conversation from already-fetched state, else fetches the current user's profile name and inserts a conversation with last_message='' and last_message_time=now(); blocked pairs are refused conversation creation server-side.
No polling exists anywhere in the messaging stack (no setInterval/refetchInterval). All updates are realtime push plus mount-time fetches.

Mark-as-read is re-triggered by the messages effect only when the last message sender_id !== user.id, preventing the user's own sends from bumping their own read receipt; unreadCount for the conversation is zeroed locally on markAsRead.
edgeCases: Sender's own message arrives via realtime — if it races the initial fetch, the dedupe check (prev.some(m => m.id === next.id)) prevents double append; otherwise the message appears only after the server round-trip + WAL event, so there is an observable latency and no optimistic UI.

If the messages INSERT succeeds but the conversations UPDATE (last_message/last_message_time) fails, the error is silently swallowed (awaited, not checked) — the message renders but the conversation preview/order/unread recompute can go stale until another conversations event fires.
markAsRead effect runs on every messages array change; guarded by messages.length === 0 return and last.sender_id !== user.id, but it can fire before the initial fetch populates messages (no-op).

Because conversations-updates refetches on ANY conversations change in the entire DB (no row filter on the table subscription), unrelated conversations being created/deleted elsewhere trigger refetches in every open client; under heavy traffic the refetch storm can drop events or cause churn in the Chats list.

Read receipts start null on conversation open (last_read RLS hides the other user's row from direct select); they only resolve once the other user upserts last_read while the channel is subscribed — so a 'delivered' state persists for previously-read messages until a fresh markAsRead event arrives.

requests-changes realtime does not work (table not replicated + no authorization branch), so a newly accepted request will not appear in the Chats companion list until the hook remounts (page navigation).
Presence only reflects users who currently have the Chat page open for that exact conversation — a user browsing the Chats list or another tab appears offline even if actively using the app.

Typing broadcasts are sent on every keystroke with a fresh channel instance and no throttle; rapid typing keeps resetting the 3s timer, and the typing indicator can persist longer than 3s. If a user navigates away mid-typing, their typing indicator can linger for up to 3s on the other side.

Attachment-only messages have empty text; the composer preview is '📷 Photo' (image) or '📎 <name>' (file), stored as last_message; text validation is skipped for attachment messages but a >2000-char text with an attachment throws a custom error.
Delete chat is a soft delete (deleted_for array) — the conversation row still exists and reappears if a new message arrives, and the RPC refuses deleting for anyone other than the authenticated self.

Multi-tab same user on the same conversation share one presence key (state[key] becomes an array) — the sync handler collapses to { online: true }, which is correct for the 'other user online' use case.
notes: Exact channel/subscription strings for the realtime migration section: (1) useChat.tsx:63-76 — `messages-${conversationId}`, postgres_changes INSERT on public.messages with filter `conversation_id=eq.${conversationId}`; (2) useChat.tsx:104-116 — `last-read-${conversationId}-${otherUserId}`, postgres_changes event '*' on public.last_read with filter `conversation_id=eq.${conversationId}`; (3) useChat.tsx:145-148 — `conversations-updates-${user.id}`, postgres_changes event '*' on public.conversations with NO filter; (4) usePresence.ts:20 — `presence-${conversationId}` with `{ config: { presence: { key: user.id } } }` handling presence sync/join/leave and broadcast 'typing' (and usePresence.ts:73 a second throwaway `presence-${conversationId}` instance that only broadcasts typing); (5) useAcceptedCompanions.ts:75-97 — `requests-changes` with two postgres_changes listeners (filters `from_user_id=eq.${user.id}` and `to_user_id=eq.${user.id}`). Real-time authorized tables (in supabase_realtime publication): messages, conversations, last_read (requests is missing). Realtime authorization policy file: supabase/migrations/20260702121413_f44b81c6-1de3-40d3-8b75-62b00342fbc4.sql. Key DB files: supabase/migrations/20251212061640_5dc954fa-b976-4b88-b0e4-bdb3250214f5.sql (messages/last_read/conversations schema + RLS), 20260618111613 (messages attachment columns), 20260618111636 (last_read REPLICA IDENTITY FULL + publication), 20260703100726 (soft_delete_conversation RPC + prevent_conversation_tamper trigger). Client file: C:/Users/sward/trainmate-v2/src/hooks/useChat.tsx, usePresence.ts, useAcceptedCompanions.ts; pages C:/Users/sward/trainmate-v2/src/pages/Chats.tsx and Chat.tsx; components TypingIndicator.tsx (presentational only), UnreadBadge.tsx, OnlineStatus.tsx (presentational; not actually used in Chat.tsx header which hand-rolls the dot), lib/chatFormat.ts (time/date formatting only). Supabase client uses default realtime config (no custom params). The migration target should preserve: topic-based per-conversation filtering, participant-only authorization for messages/last_read, self-only conversations-updates topics, REPLICA IDENTITY FULL on last_read, and the requests publication gap.
